proposal.diagnosis: The TX and RX modules use opposite bit ordering for serialization/deserialization: TX sends data_reg[0] first (which is input LSB when data_reg = {input_axi_tdata, 1'b1}), while RX shifts new rxd bits into data_reg[0] (effectively expecting MSB first). This makes the pair agree with each other but disagree with an independent LSB-first serial peer, causing both tx_bad and rx_bad to increment in the public test. Additionally, TX immediately clears tready in the same cycle it accepts input, violating the harness requirement that tready remain asserted for at least one cycle after acceptance. RX frame detection also starts with a 1/4-bit prescale and a start-bit check that can misalign sampling. Fix: make TX shift MSB-first (or RX shift LSB-first) to agree with independent LSB-first peer; keep tready asserted for one extra cycle after acceptance; align RX prescale to a full bit period and sample start bit at mid-bit.
